title: Gideon and the Static
premise: Emrys Yarrow is a clone of the murdered relay engineer Gideon Yarrow, legally bound to finish his last contract: running supply and mail along the Long Route between two colonies that severed contact after his death. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — a voice counting down from the dead relay at the edge of static-choked space — Emrys realizes Gideon's consciousness may have survived in the relay itself, and that whoever killed him is now aboard her ship as her assigned 'protector.' Racing the closing jump window, she must choose between preserving her own fragile identity and merging with the inherited memories to free Gideon's signal. She frees him by letting the relay die, exposing his killer, and choosing for the first time a self that is entirely her own.
about_author: Wendell Hartwell is a former radio technician who spent six years maintaining remote listening stations in the subarctic before turning to fiction. He writes slow-burn science fiction about people who inherit other people's unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Emrys runs the mail run between colonies Meridian and Halcyon, worlds that stopped speaking after Gideon's murder five years ago. POV: Emrys. We learn she is his clone, resented by both colonies, and bound by inheritance law to complete his contracts. Emotional beat: weary isolation, the ache of living someone else's life.

chapters.title: Children of the Static
chapters.summary: At Meridian, forty children describe an identical dream: a man's voice counting down inside white noise, calling a name only Gideon would know. The colony blames Emrys, claiming she brought his ghost with her. POV: Emrys, with a scene from a child, Sefa. Emotional beat: dread blooming into reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Inheritance Law
chapters.summary: Emrys reviews Gideon's sealed final logs under her legal rights and finds a corrupted transmission addressed to 'the one wearing my face,' warning of sabotage at Relay Nine. Her shipboard protector, Inspector Voss, insists on accompanying her. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: suspicion — Voss knows too much about the route.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: En route, Emrys attempts contact with the relay using Gideon's old frequencies. Something answers — fragments of memory only Gideon could hold: his mother's kitchen, the murder night. Voss dismisses it as echo. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness entangled; she is hearing her own stolen childhood.

chapters.title: The Man Who Guards Me
chapters.summary: Voss's behavior frays: he disables her navigation backups 'for security' and interrogates her about Gideon's private files. Emrys discovers he was the last person cleared to access Relay Nine before the murder. POV: alternating Emrys and Voss. Emotional beat: claustrophobic paranoia aboard a small ship.

chapters.title: What the Dream Wants
chapters.summary: The children's dream evolves — now it shows the relay's interior and a hidden data vault. Emrys realizes Gideon hid evidence there before dying, and the countdown is the jump window closing forever. POV: Sefa, then Emrys receiving a transmitted dream. Emotional beat: urgency; the dead are asking for help.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: A solar storm will seal the corridor to Relay Nine within days. Emrys commits to the detour against her contract terms, knowing it means forfeiting everything Gideon left her. Voss agrees to come — too readily. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Relay Nine
chapters.summary: Inside the derelict relay, Emrys finds the vault and Gideon's stored consciousness fragment, which begins overwriting her memories with his. Voss reveals himself: he killed Gideon to bury evidence of the colonies' illegal severance deal. POV: Emrys, dissolving between two identities. Emotional beat: climax of identity — who is dreaming whom?

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Voss tries to destroy the relay and Emrys with it. To broadcast the evidence, Emrys must amplify Gideon's fragment through her own neural link — sharing her body's bandwidth with the dead man one final time. The truth transmits to both colonies as Voss is caught in the blast he set. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: love against duty fulfilled at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Her Own Frequency
chapters.summary: Gideon's fragment fades, thanking her and letting go. Both colonies reopen contact, and the children's dream goes quiet. Emrys renegotiates her contract — not as Gideon's heir, but as herself, captain of her own route. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; inheritance released, identity claimed.
